```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(itsmr)
```

## Set up time series
```{r}
Z_t <- rnorm(100, 0, 2)
t <- c(1:100)

X_t <- 0.1*t + Z_t
```

## ACF Plotting
```{r}
h <- c(0:50)

acf(X_t, lag.max = 50, 
    main = expression(paste("Sample ACF of ", X[t])),
    col = "darkgray", lwd = 2)
```

This ACF has the form it does by attempting to average towards 0 for the ACF when the lag `h != 0`. At `h = 0`, clearly we see that the ACF = 1 just like with the true/theoretical ACF computed. However, at `h != 0` it isn't exactly ACF = 0 like the theoretical formula, but trends towards it and likely will have some more negative lags `h > 50` to produce an average ~= 0.
